This prompts scientists to revise or create new hypotheses, which are then rigorously tested through experiments and data analysis. If the evidence supports the hypothesis, it may lead to a groundbreaking discovery that alters our understanding of reality.

These discoveries don't necessarily negate previous truths but rather refine them within a broader, more nuanced framework.
